content.text:
Japan and Korea were being overcharged 100x because the currency lookup was case-sensitive. I fixed it in `src/lib/currency/registry.js`, and `npm test` now passes (9 of 9).

**Root cause:** `buildChargePayload` (`src/payments/gateway/payload.js`) lowercases the currency to `"jpy"` for the gateway. It then passed that lowercase code to `toMinor()`. The registry only had upper-case keys (`JPY`, `KRW`), so `"jpy"` wasn't found and fell back to the default exponent of 2. That turned ¥1,500 into 150,000. USD and EUR have exponent 2 anyway, which is why they looked fine.

**Fix:** `exponent`, `isSupported` and `symbol` in `registry.js` now look codes up case-insensitively. I fixed it there rather than in the payload code so any other caller that passes a lowercase code is also covered.

**Tests:** I added three tests to `test/charge.test.js`. They cover JPY (¥1,500 charges as 1500), KRW (₩20,000 charges as 20000), and a case-insensitive exponent lookup (`jpy` gives 0, `kwd` gives 3). With the fix reverted, all three fail.

I haven't traced the other callers (refunds, payouts, coupons). They use the same `toMinor` and now get the correct exponent whatever case their currency code arrives in.
